- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast 2–4 days after spike.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.5 to -0.5 within 3 days), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to match sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 60–70% of historical range, model often overcorrects; apply a “reversion anchor” rule: cap forecast at 65–70% of recent 10-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
